item.text:
**Assessment**
Leaning `yes on investment in foundations`, but with a major caveat: Abiy’s 2024 government pushed a broad package of infrastructure, education, health, digital, and administrative-capacity reforms, yet conflict and emergency rule still damaged the reliability of those foundations and the predictability of the operating environment.

**Accepted Claims**
- [IMF Executive Board Approves Four-Year US$3.4 billion Extended Credit Facility Arrangement for Ethiopia](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24291-ethiopia-imf-exec-board-approves-4yr-us3b-ecf-arr) | IMF | 2024-07-29 | The IMF said the homegrown reform agenda would improve governance and public service delivery, competitiveness, and the business climate, with private-sector-led growth and poverty reduction as explicit goals. This is strong evidence of an investment in productivity foundations rather than only short-term political gains. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.1`

- [The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia: Request of an Arrangement Under the Extended Credit Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/07/29/the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-request-of-an-arrangement-under-the-extended-552778) | IMF | 2024-07-29 | The staff report says HGER2.0 includes macro reforms, investment and trade reforms to boost competitiveness and entrepreneurship, productive-sector reforms to raise productivity, and public-sector reforms to improve service delivery. This directly supports the case for long-term productivity-building. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`

- [Energizing Ethiopia: New World Bank Program Expands Access to Electricity](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/04/03/energizing-afe-ethiopia-new-world-bank-program-expands-access-to-electricity) | World Bank | 2024-04-03 | The World Bank said Ethiopia’s power-sector reform program would strengthen and expand the electricity network, improve utility financial viability, and mobilize private-sector participation. That is core productivity infrastructure, not just consumption support. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`

- [Ethiopia - Governance Modernization to Enable Efficient Service Delivery Project](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099082124120033234) | World Bank | 2024-08-16 | The project’s development objective is to improve government capacity to mobilize and manage public financial and human resources efficiently, with emphasis on public administration, public finance, procurement, and core government systems. This is direct evidence of administrative-capacity building. | `5B.6`, `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [Ethiopia Digitizes 620 Public Service Institutions](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4597948) | ENA English | 2024-06-13 | The government said 620 public service institutions had been digitalized, alongside digital-skill initiatives for youth. This is concrete evidence of technology and administrative modernization aimed at productivity. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [Ethiopia's New Digital Strategy Poised to be Transformative for Government’s Digital Future: Innovation Minister](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4759694) | ENA English | 2024-07-11 | The government described a new 2024-2029 digital-government strategy as a blueprint for a digitally empowered Ethiopia developed with stakeholder input. That supports the “predictable regulation plus technology” side of the lens. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [Gov't Investing on Innovation and Technology to Ensure Quality Healthcare Services](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4118007) | ENA English | 2024-03-05 | The Ministry of Health said Ethiopia was investing in innovation and technology infrastructure, including digitization and automation in health information systems to improve quality, continuity, accountability, and learning. This is strong evidence of productivity-oriented health-system investment. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [Gov’t Vows to Strengthen Health Financing to Further Improve Ethiopia’s Health Services](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5233579) | ENA English | 2024-10-03 | The ministry said Ethiopia completed a six-year health-financing program that improved insurance coverage and reduced financial barriers to primary care, while pursuing stronger health financing. This supports human-capital and health-productivity foundations. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`

- [Breaking Barriers: Empowering Girls with Clean Water and Sanitation Facilities in Ethiopia's Schools](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/01/19/breaking-barriers-empowering-girls-with-clean-water-and-sanitation-facilities-in-ethiopias-schools) | World Bank | 2024-01-19 | The World Bank said OWNP had equipped over 5,000 schools with WASH facilities and improved attendance, especially among girls. That is a productivity foundation because it supports health, learning, and labor-force development. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.1`

- [UNICEF Leads Efforts to Ensure Education for All Children in Ethiopia](https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/press-releases/unicef-leads-efforts-ensure-education-all-children-ethiopia) | UNICEF Ethiopia | 2024 | UNICEF said it worked with the Ministry of Education on curriculum reform, teacher capacity, digital learning, and school inclusion, aiming to improve education quality and accessibility. This is positive evidence for human-capital investment. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.1`

- [Building a Strong Foundation to Improve Learning Outcomes in Ethiopia](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/09/05/building-a-strong-foundation-to-improve-learning-outcomes-in-afe-ethiopia) | World Bank | 2024-09-05 | The World Bank said GEQIP-E supported teacher training, tablets, assessment tools, textbooks, and digital skills for teachers, and had already trained over 102,000 teachers. This is direct evidence of education-capacity investment. | `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.1`

- [Bringing back more schools, health facilities to life in Tigray](https://ethiopia.un.org/en/261479-bringing-back-more-schools-health-facilities-life-tigray) | United Nations in Ethiopia | 2024-02-23 | The government-backed 3R4CACE project reconstructed health centers, schools, and WASH facilities in conflict-affected areas, restoring services for hundreds of thousands of people. This is tangible infrastructure repair and administrative recovery. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- [Conflict in Ethiopia has had a devastating impact on Education](https://www.unesco.org/gem-report/en/2026-gem-report-country-case-studies/ethiopia?hub=1074) | UNESCO | 2024/2026 country case study page | UNESCO says conflict reversed educational progress, the number of out-of-school children remained very high, and education spending had fallen to 2.3% of GDP in 2024. This is strong negative evidence that the foundations were still badly damaged despite reform efforts. | `5B.6`, `4B.10`, `5B.3`

- [Ethiopia extends state of emergency in Amhara](https://kelo.com/2024/02/02/ethiopia-extends-state-of-emergency-in-amhara/) | Reuters | 2024-02-02 | Reuters reported parliament extended emergency rule amid insurgency, deaths, and abuse allegations. This is negative evidence for predictable regulation and long-term investment conditions because it shows a coercive, unstable operating environment. | `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `4B.10`, `5B.4`

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence of investment in infrastructure, education, health, and digital/state capacity.
- I did not find equally strong 2024 evidence that these investments were already translating into broad, economy-wide productivity gains.
- The main drag is conflict: emergency rule, school disruption, and regional instability continued to erode the predictability and durability of the environment those investments need.
